thread:
kevin: heads up — operator found an odd race when doing a full region drain for a tenant with residency constraints. details below. :wave:

kevin: steps we ran: cordon region -> prewarm standby -> issue handoff -> swap leases. on swap we saw ~120ms of split responses where reads hit both old and new region.

sarah: can you paste the operator logs? curious if lease revoke ack got delayed.

kevin: snippet from operator logs: `lease_swap request id=tn-42 from region-us -> region-eu; sent revoke to proxy; got ack from dataplane after 1.2s`

maria: 1.2s ack is large. did proxy actually drain connections or just ack it?

kevin: proxy acked before fully draining. reason: our proxy sends ack on receipt of swap message, not after in-flight drain finished. operator assumed ack==quiesced. mismatch.

andrew: that's a contract bug. operator needs a stronger handshake (revoked -> drained -> final-confirm). current two-stage is insufficient. propose introducing a "drain_complete" state.

liz: agree. also legal/residency teams will freak if there are simultaneous writes during the swap. we need an explicit window where writes are rejected (or forwarded) until final-confirm.

maria: tradeoff: long reject window hurts latency for bursty clients. alternate: allow readonly on new region + buffer writes in escrow with strict idempotency keys.

kevin: rough proposal: handshake states: PREPARE -> PROXY_ACK -> PROXY_DRAINED -> OP_FINALIZE. and add a header `X-Region-Quiesced: true|false` that proxies set when fully drained. operator waits for PROXY_DRAINED before committing leases.

andrew: downside: proxies must be able to report drain progress reliably. we need telemetry + backpressure so operator can escalate if a proxy stalls. maybe exponential backoff and automatic revert.

liz: also need to consider function callers and streamable responses (long-lived SSE/websocket). those clients might keep connections open for minutes. how do we enforce drain?

maria: we should use a soft-cutover approach for streams: mark region as DRAINING and attach `retry-after` hint, continue serving but stop accepting new persistent sessions. existing sessions are signaled to reconnect to the new endpoint via room-level hint.

kevin: example header we can use for final-confirm:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Region-Drain-Status: drained
X-Region-Quiesced: true
```

andrew: operator CLI for manual swap prototype:

```
redwood-operator swap-lease --tenant tn-42 --from us --to eu --mode staged --timeout 90s
```

liz: how do we handle cross-region in-flight writes that are not idempotent? we need a fallback model. options: 1) synchronous forward to old region until finalize, 2) temporary escrow queue + at-least-once apply + dedupe layer, 3) reject non-idempotent writes during swap.

maria: I'd vote for (2) with a short TTL on escrow and strong idempotency keys. we already have per-tenant dedupe tokens in the pipeline.

kevin: ok - add to proposal: escrow service runs per-tenant (or shard) with TTL=30s default; operator can extend TTL when necessary. telemetry exposes escrow queue depth. if depth>threshold -> abort swap and revert.

andrew: we also need a control-plane signal so downstream billing/analytics know the tenant was in a transient escrow state. add event `tenant.swap.escrowed` with durations.

liz: one more thing: privacy/regulatory boundary. if tenant opted into data residency, we must never forward writes to non-resident region. so for those tenants, swap must be done via pre-copy + validation not forward/escrow. that constraint should be enforced by a preflight check.

kevin: right. enforce preflight: operator refuses swap if tenant.residency=EU_ONLY and target is non-EU. add explicit abort with error code `E_RESIDENCY_VIOLATION`.

maria: we should document the interface spec for proxies/operator: minimal message types `lease_swap`, `lease_revoke`, `drain_state`, `drain_progress`, `drain_complete`. all messages idempotent and signed.

kevin: i'll open an RFC PR with a finite state machine diagram and sample messages. TL;DR of proposed contract: make ack mean "received", not "complete"; add explicit `drain_complete` before finalizing leases; use escrow for non-idempotent writes with TTL and metrics gating; block any swap that violates residency.

andrew: +1 on the contract. can we get ops-bot to alert if operator retries exceed 3x?

ops-bot: noted. adding alert rule: `operator.swap.retries >= 3 -> pager oncall-eng` :bell:

liz: thanks, team. can we aim to land RFC by EOD Friday? need to present to legal next week.

kevin: will do. I'll add the small operator CLI prototype and the FSM draft to the RFC. ping me with any edgecases. :thumbsup:
